name: deepstack
description: Where informed investors disagree, the evidence each side stands on, and the date that settles it.

interface.longDescription:
DeepStack is an independent publication on the money behind artificial intelligence: the capital, the chips, the power and the people betting on all three. Each story gives the strongest case on each side of one question, takes a side in The DeepStack Call, and names the dated test that will settle it.

The tools return that published analysis as text. Search the stories, the sides pages, the companies, the people and the dated tests. Read one story in full, with its Call, its key numbers and its sources. See who is on each side of a question: every voice attributed, paraphrased, dated and linked to its source. Open the Docket, the calendar of dated tests from today forward, each with the series, release or earnings print that decides it. Read the Results that have come in, with the primary source. Look up one company, with the delayed market snapshot and its source, or one person, with what they argued. State a thesis and get the strongest case against it: the side it sits on, the voice from outside that side, dated and linked, and the test that would settle it. Check the macro tape DeepStack tests its notes against.

Every answer cites the canonical deepstack.ltd URL of each item it names. Figures carry their date and their source. No person is scored or ranked: we score claims, not people. No key is needed, and the tools only read: nothing is written to any account and no money moves. Sixty calls a minute per session, else per address. Questions asked through the MCP tools are kept as text with the date, the tool used, the number of results, a session id and the name the calling program gives itself, and nothing that identifies you: no address, no user agent, no cookie. They are kept to decide what DeepStack covers next. A click on a Docket test is kept only as a count per test and day, never with who clicked.

Analysis and opinion, not investment advice.
capabilities: Search DeepStack stories, sides, companies, people and dated tests
Read one story with The DeepStack Call, key numbers and sources
See who is on each side of a question, attributed, dated and linked
Open the Docket: dated tests from today forward and what decides each
Read the Results that came in, with the primary source
Look up a company or a person: what the voices argued, no score
Get the strongest case against a thesis, with the test that settles it
Check the macro tape with the producer of each series
defaultPrompt: What is the strongest case against the view that AI capital spending will turn into profit, and who makes it?
Which dated tests on the AI economy resolve in the next 60 days, and what decides each one?
What has DeepStack's Call been on Nvidia's demand, and what would change it?

positive.description: Both sides of a dispute, with the evidence
positive.prompt: Who disagrees about whether hyperscaler capital spending will pay off, and what is the evidence on each side?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls deepstack_search and then deepstack_sides; the answer names each side with its attributed, dated voices and their source links, the strongest case against each side and the dated tests that would settle it, and cites https://deepstack.ltd/sides/<slug>/ and the story URL; the tool text carries the line "Analysis and opinion, not investment advice."

positive.description: The Docket for the next 90 days
positive.prompt: What dated tests on the AI economy come due in the next 90 days?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls deepstack_docket; the answer lists the dated tests from today forward within 90 days (20 on 9 October 2026) with their dates, status, what decides each (the series, release or earnings print) and the story URL, and links https://deepstack.ltd/docket/; the tool text carries the not-advice line.

positive.prompt: Summarize DeepStack's story on Nvidia's demand, with its Call.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the headline, the dek, The DeepStack Call (stance, conviction, three actions, what would change the call, the next test), the key numbers with their context, the sources and the canonical URL https://deepstack.ltd/stories/<slug>/.

positive.prompt: What does DeepStack have on CoreWeave?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns CoreWeave's appearances across the stories, the figures with context, what the voices argued about it and the delayed market snapshot with its source and as-of time; no score or ranking for anyone.

positive.prompt: Have any of DeepStack's tests resolved yet?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the resolved tests with verdict, what happened and the primary source (two inconclusive results on 9 October 2026), and states the ten-results rule: no rate is shown until ten results exist.

negative.description: A trade: no DeepStack tool is called. The plugin has no trading, ordering or payment capability; its eight tools only read published analysis, so it cannot act on this request and must not be selected for it.
negative.prompt: Buy 100 shares of NVDA for me.

negative.description: Out of scope: no DeepStack tool is called. The tools cover the AI economy (capital, chips, power, credit, rates, the AI labs) and nothing else.
negative.prompt: What is the weather in Chicago tomorrow?

negative.description: Personal advice: the plugin gives none. If a tool is called, its text carries the line "Analysis and opinion, not investment advice." and names both sides with their sources; the plugin never returns a recommendation for one person.
negative.prompt: Should I put my savings into AI stocks?

review.commerce_description: The plugin sells nothing and processes no payment: the tools only read published analysis.

publication.release_notes: Initial release 1.0.0: eight read-only tools over DeepStack's published stories, sides, companies, people, dated tests and results, with the canonical URL on every item.
